entry_state: Chapter14 closes with a bounded development corpus and provisional workload limits. Complete acquisition slots do not establish complete disclosure packages or historical availability. Engineering release, accounting acceptance, forecast promotion and human comprehension require distinct additional evidence. The body now hands the reader to appendices that give portable operation and historical-core references.
exit_state: AppendixA introduces specified portable exchanges under the common envelope. Corporate, joined-company and real-source packages bind inputs, schemas, references and before/after worlds while retaining finite documentary scope. The operation registry begins with source preparation and review proposals; neither admits a financial claim. Review commitment and the remaining operations follow.
findings: The appendix declares its lookup role and points to the body's common request envelope; specified exchanges are not described as deployed endpoints.
The corporate package retains the smaller debt-text frontend, complete company typed input and unresolved coverage, with invalid decoding distinguished from a later transaction conflict.
Joined-company receipts require both legal journals, full dates and cash origins. Narrow migration preserves subsequent-operation quantities and refuses an owner substitution as lossless migration.
The real-source family remains an unresolved question about issuer histories. Completed reported-token subqueries do not upgrade the connected partial result, and no mutation is claimed.
